**No one has walked on Mars, so the question rests on a false premise.** No crewed mission has launched to Mars, and there is no "first" person to name.

I did not use the deep-research skill's subagent and file workflow. It needs shell commands and local files, which you ruled out, so I ran two retrievals directly.

- No human has landed on or walked on Mars. NASA's page lists Mars's population as "Zero" and treats crewed missions as future goals. https://www.nasa.gov/humans-in-space/humans-to-mars/
- NASA says it is working to send astronauts to Mars "as early as the 2030s." Its example round-trip mission is in 2039. The page says it is being updated for recent Artemis changes, so these dates may shift. https://www.nasa.gov/humans-in-space/humans-to-mars/
- Mars exploration so far has been robotic only. For example, China's Tianwen-1 lander and Zhurong rover landed in May 2021. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_crewed_Mars_mission_plans (the search summary mentioned this landing, but I did not open the page)
- China has said it plans a first crewed Mars mission around 2033. This comes from a 2021 article, so the date may be out of date. https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/24/china-plans-for-first-manned-mission-to-mars-in-2033
- SpaceX reportedly told investors in February 2026 that it would prioritize the Moon first and attempt Mars later. This comes from a fan wiki citing the Wall Street Journal, so I'd treat it as weak evidence. https://starship-spacex.fandom.com/wiki/Mars_Missions

I checked only a NASA page and search summaries. I did not open the other pages. I also did not look for news after the NASA page was last updated, so I can't rule out a very recent mission. Nothing I found suggests one.
